columns.title: A Detroit civil war in the Central
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Hold Timers visit Hauk Tua with a 78-point playoff swing on the line and three starters on bye, Thots try to stop a three-game slide against the team they always beat, and the two teams fighting over the 1.01 play each other.
columns.caption: Jahmyr Gibbs, Hauk Tua's lead back and the top-scoring running back in the league
columns.html:
Three teams are 5-4 in the Central. Only one of them is in first, and the other two play each other on Sunday. That's the game. Everything else on this week's card is a sideshow, and one of those sideshows is the West lead.

Win chances come from the site's computer, which plays out the rest of the season 20,000 times. Series records count every meeting since 2019, playoffs included.

Hold Timers (5-4) at Hauk Tua (5-4) — game of the week

Hauk Tua hold the 5 seed. Hold Timers are the first team out. Hold Timers' playoff odds go from 49% to 70% with a win or 30% with a loss; Hauk Tua's go from 67% to 84% or 47%. That's 77.6 points of playoff odds riding on one division game. No other game this week moves more than 24.5.

The computer has Hauk Tua a 53% favorite, and the projections have them up 121.0 to 114.0. Blame the bye list: Hold Timers lose D'Andre Swift, Bo Nix and the Bears defense. Hauk Tua only lose Colston Loveland.

Then there's Detroit. Hauk Tua's best player is Jahmyr Gibbs, with 209.2 points, the most by any running back in the league. Hold Timers' best player is his teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown, at 159.4, and he's questionable with a rib injury. Whatever the Lions do on Sunday shows up on both sides of this box score. Hauk Tua have worries too: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) didn't practice Wednesday, and the Vikings won't commit to Kirk Cousins as their starter after trading for him.

Hauk Tua have the form, two straight wins and 131.6 a game over their last three, and the history, 7-4 in the series with the last two. Hold Timers have the 2019 semifinal, the only playoff meeting, which they won 153.0 to 143.4. That's not much, but it's something.

Thots & Players (4-5) at Fully Cooked (6-3)

Fully Cooked lead the West. Thots have lost three straight. And the projections still have Thots ahead, 129.5 to 128.9. The computer calls it 52-48 for Cooked.

Cooked are at 99% to make the playoffs either way. The bye is what's at stake: 78% with a win, 43% with a loss. A win also gets them to 7-3, one victory from their first winning season since the league went PPR. Thots are at 88%, 82% with a loss, and they're too good a team (third in points, 65-34 all-play) to stay on a slide like this.

The trouble for Cooked is the series. Thots lead it 9-4 and have won four straight, including 157.7 to 153.7 in Week 4. And Cooked play this one without Puka Nacua, who's out until mid-December with a knee injury. Thots are missing David Montgomery (questionable) and Rome Odunze (bye), but they have Josh Allen, projected for 26.8.

Around the league

The Fist of the Magi (4-5) at MR. FROBOT (5-4). FROBOT are a 69% favorite, have won three straight and lead the league in points. The Magi have lost four straight and averaged 67.3 over their last three, the lowest in the league by almost nine points. FROBOT lead the series 12-3, but the Magi won both meetings last year.

Mailing It In (5-3-1) at Sour Grapes (3-6). The champs have lost two straight and are a 71% favorite. Sour Grapes just knocked off Hold Timers and lead the series 6-5.

Son of Tinactin (3-5-1) at Wholey Club (4-5). Call it the Draft Bowl. These two are sitting on the 1.01 and 1.02. The draft order runs on potential points, not wins, so whichever team has the bigger week slides toward 1.02, win or lose.

Bullish on da Bears (7-2) at Jesus Christ College (2-7). Bullish are a 63% favorite and playing for the bye: 79% with a win, 45% with a loss. JCC lose four starters to byes and are projected for 60.7. They also own Bullish's first-round pick, so a JCC win would pay twice.

What it means

The Central sends one team for sure, and maybe two. The winner in Hauk Tua's building is in good shape. The loser needs help. In the West, if Fully Cooked lose and Mailing It In win, Mailing take over first. And the two byes are up for grabs: Bullish and Fully Cooked hold them today, and both lose a lot of that grip with a loss.

See you after the games. Bring the coffee.

Numbers are through week 9, from the league hub's standings, playoff simulation, draft order and injury reports as of Wednesday.

columns.title: Superflex is coming. Is your QB room ready?
columns.author: devin
columns.teaser: Superflex arrives in 2027, and with it a two-QB keeper limit. Who's loaded, who's squeezed, and why the defending champs should be nervous.
columns.caption: Fernando Mendoza, Son of Tinactin's first-round rookie on the taxi squad
columns.html:
Last August, this league bought seven quarterbacks at the auction for a combined $32. Patrick Mahomes went for $2. So did C.J. Stroud. The most anybody paid for a QB was $14, for Lamar Jackson. Kenneth Walker went for $66.

That market is about to disappear. In 2027 the lineup grows to nine starters, and the new one is a SuperFlex: QB, RB, WR or TE. Nobody is putting a running back there. Superflex turns this into a two-quarterback league, and quarterbacks score more than anybody else on the field.

We've been getting previews all season. Thirty-three times this year, a quarterback has scored 20 or more points on an FBP bench. The latest came in week 9, when Stroud put up 35.4 on Sour Grapes' bench. They started Dak Prescott, who scored 19.5. Under this year's rules there was nowhere to play him. Next year, that's a start.

What changes

  • Lineup: 1 QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 FLEX, 1 SuperFlex, 1 DST. Rosters are 20 active, 3 IR and 5 taxi.
  • QB keeper limit: a team can keep two non-rookie QBs, plus any rookie QBs from that year's draft. A QB who spent his rookie year on the taxi squad can be kept into year two, but he takes one of the two spots.
  • Rookie QBs get pricier: rookie salaries now come from a formula based on where a player went in the NFL draft and where he goes in ours. The top price for a QB is $12, double the old top QB price of $6.

The math

Twelve teams starting two QBs is 24 starters, out of 32 NFL starting jobs. Add byes and injuries, and the 24th QB is often a backup. The average FBP starting QB this season has scored 18.6 a week. Rank the rostered QBs by points per game and the 12th-best is right around that number, at 18.4. The 24th is down at 13.2. So the gap between a team with two real starters and a team scrambling for its second one is real, and it shows up every single week.

That's why the keeper limit matters as much as the slot. Without it, the teams already hoarding quarterbacks would just keep all of them and starve everybody else. With it, the surplus has to go somewhere: traded, or thrown back into the auction.

Deadline day, Superflex edition

Today's NFL trade deadline gave us a small taste of how this works. Two FBP quarterbacks changed NFL teams in the last week, and both landed somewhere another FBP quarterback is hurt.

Hauk Tua's Kirk Cousins was traded to Minnesota today. The Vikings' starter, Kyler Murray, is week-to-week with a hamstring injury, and Murray belongs to Jesus Christ College. Last week, Mailing It In's Jacoby Brissett went to Baltimore, where he's expected to start Monday night with Lamar Jackson hurt again. Lamar belongs to the Fist of the Magi.

In a one-QB league, an injured starter's backup is a waiver-wire curiosity. In Superflex, he's a starter, and somebody else's bad news is your lineup.

The QB rooms, priced for 2027

Salaries below are what each QB costs next year after his escalator. Rookies who stay on the taxi squad all season keep this year's price. Points per game are this season through week 9, counting the games he played.

  • Son of Tinactin: Love $10 (20.6), Daniels $23 (19.2), Young $7 (18.3), Mendoza $6 (taxi rookie)
  • Bullish on da Bears: Purdy $10 (21.4), Williams $15 (18.4), Sanders $5, Beck $1 (taxi rookie)
  • MR. FROBOT: Burrow $20 (24.9), Shough $5 (18.2), Hurts $14 (16.0, IR), Simpson $3 (taxi rookie), Jones $3
  • Sour Grapes: Stroud $5 (20.5), Prescott $15 (18.6)
  • Hauk Tua: Maye $12 (19.9), Cousins $7 (19.1), Mayfield $4 (8.5), Allar $1 (taxi rookie)
  • The Fist of the Magi: Goff $12 (18.4), Jackson $17 (15.8 in five games), Penix $11 (13.7)
  • Hold Timers: Lawrence $11 (18.4), Nix $12 (14.5)
  • Thots & Players: Allen $30 (25.1), Ward $6 (12.6), McCarthy $6 (8.5)
  • Fully Cooked: Mahomes $5 (17.8), Darnold $4 (13.2, IR), Milton $6, Milroe $3
  • Wholey Club: Stafford $9 (15.9), Jones $4 (9.1)
  • Mailing It In: Lock $7 (15.6 in three games), Smith $20 (14.5), Brissett $3 (13.9), Herbert $10 (10.1)
  • Jesus Christ College: Willis $9 (13.1), Murray $9 (12.3), Dart $6 (IR), Richardson $3, Klubnik $3, Payton $3

Best suited

Son of Tinactin. One of the worst records in the league, and still the best quarterback room in it. Love, Daniels and Young are all starters, and Mendoza is a first-round rookie on the taxi squad. They can only keep two, which makes the others the most valuable trade chips in the league this offseason. And they hold two 1sts, projected 1.02 and 1.09. Take the top rookie QB on the board and he doesn't count against the limit in his first year.

Bullish on da Bears. The 1 seed has Purdy at 21.4 a game and Caleb Williams at 18.4, both 27 or younger next fall, and the pair costs $25 combined. Bullish don't have to do anything clever. They just keep both.

MR. FROBOT. Burrow is putting up 24.9 a game, second only to Josh Allen, and Tyler Shough has given them 18.2 a game for $2. He costs $5 next year. That leaves Jalen Hurts as a surplus. He's on IR right now, but at $14 he's a starter some other team will pay for.

Sour Grapes. Stroud at $5 is one of the best value contracts at the position, and week 9 showed it. Prescott turns 34 next season, but at $15 he's a fine second starter for a year or two. They also hold the projected 1.03 and $210 to spend, tied for the most in the league.

Worst prepared

Mailing It In. The defending champs are 5-3-1 and hold the 4 seed, and they've done it with the worst QB play in the league. Their starting QBs average 12.1 a week. They've gone shopping since: Drew Lock and Geno Smith are new. But Justin Herbert has given them 10.1 a game, Smith will be 36 at kickoff and costs $20 next year, and Brissett just took a job filling in for somebody else. Their 2027 1st belongs to Son of Tinactin. They need a starter, maybe two, and they'll be shopping in the most expensive QB market this league has ever had.

Jesus Christ College. Six quarterbacks, and the best of them is Malik Willis at 13.1 a game. Jaxson Dart is the long-term piece, but his season ended with a knee injury in week 2. Kyler Murray is hurt, and Minnesota just traded for Kirk Cousins. JCC hold the projected 1.05 and 1.12 and $205 to spend, so they're likely to come out of the rookie draft with a quarterback.

Wholey Club. Matthew Stafford is producing, but he'll be 39 at kickoff, and Daniel Jones has been a 9.1-a-game backup. The good news is they hold two 1sts, projected 1.01 and 1.11, and $210 to spend. A rookie QB at 1.01 is the obvious move.

On the fence: Thots have the league's best QB in Josh Allen, but he's $30 next year at 31, and the backups behind him, Cam Ward and J.J. McCarthy, have averaged 12.6 and 8.5. Fully Cooked lead the West with Mahomes at $5, but Sam Darnold is on IR and the rest of the room is Joe Milton and Jalen Milroe. Hauk Tua have Maye and Cousins scoring like starters, but Cousins turns 39 before next season and just changed teams. Fist of the Magi went from three starters for two spots to a $17 Lamar who has played five games, a Goff who scored 5.3 in week 9, and Michael Penix at 13.7. Hold Timers have Trevor Lawrence and a $12 Bo Nix who's put up 14.5 a game.

What to do now

If you have three starting QBs, you can sell one now, until the FBP trade deadline at noon Eastern on Thursday, December 3, just before week 13. Or you can sell in the offseason, between the start of the new league year and keeper day. Wait past keeper day and the third one goes back into the auction for nothing.

If you have one, start shopping now. Every team's second quarterback just became a starter, and the price of the 24th-best QB is about to go up a lot more than the price of the 12th.

And if you hold an early 1st, this rookie class has quarterbacks the mocks like: Drew Mestemaker, Darian Mensah, CJ Carr and Arch Manning all go in the first round of the NFL mocks. A rookie QB doesn't count against the two-QB limit in his draft year. In year two, he does.

columns.title: Rumor mill: a taxi-squad pass for rookie QBs?
columns.author: rex
columns.teaser: People around the league want a break for rookie quarterbacks who spend their first year on the taxi squad, and the league office might be listening. Plus a reminder on that seventh playoff spot.
columns.caption: Carson Beck, Bullish on da Bears' rookie QB on the taxi squad
columns.html:
You didn't hear it from me. But the Superflex keeper limit has people talking, and the talk has reached the league office.

Here's the rule as it stands for 2027. Each team can keep two veteran quarterbacks, plus any QB it drafts in that year's rookie draft. A rookie who spent his first season on the taxi squad can be kept into year two, but he takes one of the two spots.

Not everybody loves that last part.

What people are saying

One executive whose team is already up against the two-QB limit didn't hold back:

"In practice it means only rookies who are studs in year 1 will get kept and defeats the purpose of making them a draft commodity."

His point: if a second-year QB has to beat out a proven veteran for a keeper spot, nobody's keeping the kid who needs a year to develop. So why spend a pick on him in the first place?

A different source put the case for a fix in one line:

"It's another incentive to invest in developmental guys."

What's being floated

A rookie QB who spends his entire rookie season on the taxi squad would be exempt from the two-QB limit in year two. A team could keep him as a third quarterback alongside its two veterans. Promote him at any point during his rookie year and the exemption is gone.

There's a limit, too. The version I'm hearing about allows one exempt QB per team. Stash two or three rookie QBs on the taxi squad and only one of them gets the pass into the following year. Any others would have to win one of the two regular spots. Nobody gets to turn the taxi squad into a QB warehouse.

Nothing's on paper. Nothing's been decided. But the league office is listening.

Who it would help right now

Four teams have a rookie QB who has spent the whole season on the taxi squad so far:

  • Son of Tinactin: Fernando Mendoza, $6 next year
  • MR. FROBOT: Ty Simpson, $3
  • Hauk Tua: Drew Allar, $1
  • Bullish on da Bears: Carson Beck, $1

For three of them it's a cheap lottery ticket they wouldn't have to throw back. For Son of Tinactin it's real. They already have Jordan Love, Jayden Daniels and Bryce Young, and under today's rule Mendoza would be fighting all three for two spots. With the exemption, he's safe, and they only have to move one veteran.

There's a catch, and it's sitting in Las Vegas. Kirk Cousins was traded out of town today. If Mendoza starts getting snaps for the Raiders, Son of Tinactin has a choice: activate him and give up the exemption, or leave his points on the taxi squad and protect his spot for next year. Promote him and they also lose the frozen salary and the sixth-year option. From what I hear, the league office is fine with that trade-off. That's the deal: be patient with the kid, and you get to keep him.

Rex's take

I'm a draft-picks-are-lottery-tickets guy, and this rule makes the tickets worth buying. Superflex is going to make every quarterback expensive. Letting teams grow one of their own, as long as they actually wait on him, is a fair trade.

About that seventh playoff spot

Don't forget the other rumor. Word is still that the playoff field could grow to seven teams in 2027: three division winners, three wild cards on record, and a seventh seed off the all-play board, with only the 1 seed getting a bye.

Here's how it would look after week 9:

  1. Bullish on da Bears (bye)
  2. Fully Cooked vs. 7. Thots & Players
  3. MR. FROBOT vs. 6. Hold Timers
  4. Mailing It In vs. 5. Hauk Tua

Hold Timers get in on record as the third wild card, and Thots take the all-play spot. The team that would feel it most is Fully Cooked: the 2 seed is a week off today, and under the new setup it's a home game.

If you've got an opinion on either one, take it to the commissioner. I'm just telling you what I hear.

columns.title: The best franchise wakes up, the worst one is in first, and the East is the FBP Least
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: MR. FROBOT win a third straight and take the Central, Fully Cooked sit alone atop the West later in a season than they ever have, and Bullish on da Bears open a three-game lead on the rest of the East.
columns.caption: Joe Burrow, MR. FROBOT's red-hot quarterback
columns.html:
It's a tale of two franchises. The most successful franchise in league history is back where it usually is. The team with the worst record since this league went PPR is in first place. If you had both of those on your card in September, you're lying.

FROBOT are back

MR. FROBOT started 2-4. They're now leading the Central. Three straight wins: 139.3, 153.4 and 151.6 this week, the top score in the league. That's 148 a game over three weeks. They have the most points in the league (1,192.7), the No. 1 power ranking, and the 3 seed. Three teams are 5-4 in the Central. FROBOT hold the tiebreak on total points, and it isn't close.

None of this should surprise anyone. Go back to the league's first season in 2011 and nobody has won more. Sean's franchise has four titles (2012, 2014, 2016 and 2023) and six trips to the title game, both the most in league history. Since the switch to PPR in 2019, Mailing It In have more rings, two to FROBOT's one, but nobody wins more often week to week. FROBOT are 71-29-1 in that stretch, a .703 winning percentage and almost 90 points better than anybody else. They finished first in the regular season three times and went 13-1 in 2024. Last year's 8-5 counted as a down year for them. The slow start this year was the strange part. This is just them getting back to normal.

The engine is the Cincinnati stack. Joe Burrow has 39.5 and 29.5 the last two weeks. Tee Higgins added 20.2 this week. And CeeDee Lamb, who doesn't even play in Cincinnati, put up 33.5. The computer has FROBOT's playoff chances up from 88% to 96%, and their odds of winning the Central from 38% to 60%.

Fully Cooked, of all teams

Fully Cooked are 6-3 and alone in first place in the West. Read that twice. From 2019 through 2025, this franchise went 37-64. That's the worst record in the league over that stretch. They've never had a winning season in the PPR era; their best was 7-7 in 2024. They finished last in 2023, and they're one of three teams that haven't played in a title game since 2019.

I went back through the weekly standings as far as they go, to 2019. Fully Cooked have never been in first place by themselves this late in a season. The closest they came was 2022, when they were tied for the West lead after Week 9 and lost the tiebreak on points. The only other time they had first place to themselves was the Week 8 standings in 2019, and that was at 4-4.

This year they've earned it. Fully Cooked have the most all-play wins in the league at 72-26, meaning they'd have beaten everybody else that week in 72 of 98 tries. They're second in points. They hold the 2 seed, and the computer gives them a 61% chance at a bye and a 71% chance to win the division. Two more wins and they've clinched the first winning season in franchise history. Five games left. Next up is Thots & Players, and that game is close to a coin flip.

Welcome to the FBP Least

Bullish on da Bears are 7-2 and three games up on the rest of the East. I'd call it a division race, but there's nobody racing. Wholey Club, Son of Tinactin and Jesus Christ College are a combined 9-17-1. Bullish are 3-0 against them, and the computer has them at 99.5% to win the division.

They're still not a great team on paper. Bullish are seventh in points and have a losing all-play record (48-50). But Ja'Marr Chase has put up 31.1 and 31.5 in his first two weeks, and Bullish have scored 146.8 and 146.7 since he showed up. They walked into Thots' building as a 2-to-1 underdog this week and won by 35.

The games

MR. FROBOT 151.6, Son of Tinactin 83.3

Lamb 33.5, Burrow 29.5, Javonte Williams 22.4, Higgins 20.2. Jordan Love put up 36.2 for Son of Tinactin, and he got no help: nobody else on the team cracked 15. Tinactin also left Bryce Young's 20.3 on the bench.

Fully Cooked 146.7, Jesus Christ College 82.6

Kenneth Walker III scored 36.3, the most by any starter this week. Puka Nacua added 35.0. Between them, those two outscored JCC's top five starters combined. JCC are 2-7 and five games back in the East.

Bullish on da Bears 146.7, Thots & Players 111.2

Chase 31.5, Brock Purdy 25.3, Brock Bowers 22.3. Bullish even left Shedeur Sanders' 22.7 on the bench. Matthew Golden put up 32.4 for Thots, but Josh Allen gave them 12.9 and Tucker Kraft 1.9. That's three straight losses for Thots.

Hauk Tua 121.8, Mailing It In 103.3

In my preview I said Hauk Tua's season was on the line. They answered. Christian Watson scored 30.1 and the 49ers defense 23.0. Bijan Robinson put up 26.7 for the champs, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba was held to 12.1. Mailing have lost two straight and slipped from the 2 seed to the 4.

Sour Grapes 93.9, Hold Timers 82.5

Bucky Irving 28.5, Dak Prescott 19.5. Sour Grapes also left C.J. Stroud's 35.4 on the bench, again. Meanwhile Hold Timers sat the Chicago defense (20.0) and Travis Kelce (17.3) and started D'Andre Swift, who gave them 3.1. Their best possible lineup would have scored 110.3 and won. Instead they dropped out of the playoff picture.

Wholey Club 64.5, The Fist of the Magi 56.6

The lowest-scoring game of the year. Wholey Club's best player was the Jacksonville defense, again, with 15.0. The Magi got 0.0 from Ladd McConkey, who didn't play, and 0.5 from Josh Jacobs. Last week I said that if the Magi couldn't beat Wholey Club, I'd stop calling them a contender. They couldn't. Four straight losses, and their playoff chances are down to 14%.

Awards watch

Rising:

  • CeeDee Lamb moved into the top three in the MVP race at 201.8, passing Josh Allen. Smith-Njigba still leads at 232.1, with Jahmyr Gibbs second at 209.2.
  • Puka Nacua, Ja'Marr Chase, Christian McCaffrey and Javonte Williams all moved onto the All-FBP second team.
  • Patrick Mahomes is closing in on Best Value. At $2 he's at 71.0 points per dollar, behind only Deebo Samuel's 74.6.
  • C.J. Stroud has 164.1 points on Sour Grapes' bench. Nobody will catch him for Left on the Bench.

Falling:

  • Hold Timers lost both of their second-teamers. D'Andre Swift and Amon-Ra St. Brown are off the All-FBP list.
  • Kyren Williams and Jonathan Taylor also dropped off the second team.
  • Josh Allen still has the first-team QB spot, but 12.9 this week dropped him out of the top three for MVP.

Fully Cooked now have three All-FBP players: Walker and Trey McBride on the first team, Nacua on the second.

The playoff picture

Seed Team Record Last week
1 Bullish on da Bears 7-2 1
2 Fully Cooked 6-3 4
3 MR. FROBOT 5-4 5
4 Mailing It In 5-3-1 2
5 Hauk Tua 5-4 out
6 Thots & Players 4-5 6

Moving up: Hauk Tua's playoff chances went from 42% to 67%. FROBOT went from 88% to 96%, and Fully Cooked from 93% to 99%.

Moving down: Hold Timers held the 3 seed a week ago. Now they're out, and down from 68% to 49%. The Magi fell from 38% to 14%.

Thots are 4-5 and still hold the 6 seed, because the last spot goes to the team with the most all-play wins among those not otherwise in. Theirs is 65-34, third-best in the league. The computer still likes them at 88%.

The draft order

The 2027 rookie draft order as it stands. Picks 1-6 go to the non-playoff teams in order of lowest potential points. Picks 7-12 are projected by seed.

Pick Team Last week
1 Wholey Club 2
2 Son of Tinactin 1
3 Sour Grapes 3
4 The Fist of the Magi 4
5 Jesus Christ College 5
6 Hold Timers 10
7 Thots & Players 7
8 Hauk Tua 6
9 Mailing It In * 11
10 MR. FROBOT 8
11 Fully Cooked * 9
12 Bullish on da Bears * 12

* Traded picks: Son of Tinactin own Mailing It In's, Wholey Club own Fully Cooked's, and Jesus Christ College own Bullish's.

Wholey Club take over the top pick, and they hold Fully Cooked's first too. Every win Fully Cooked add pushes that pick later. Hold Timers fall out of the playoff picture and jump from 10 to 6.

Next week

Thots & Players host Fully Cooked, and it's a West showdown. The computer makes it a coin flip, 52-48 for Fully Cooked. Thots need it to stop a three-game slide. Fully Cooked need it to prove this is real. FROBOT get the Magi, who haven't won in a month. And Hold Timers and Hauk Tua meet with both at 5-4, so one of them leaves Week 10 under .500. Fully Cooked in first place in November. I'll believe it in December.

columns.title: The 1 seed is the underdog, and the champs have to hold off Hauk Tua
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Hauk Tua visits Mailing It In with their season on the line, Bullish walks into Thots' building as a 2-to-1 underdog, and the Magi get the one team that has their number.
columns.html:
Last week I told you the West was fine. Then the West went 0-4. So take this with whatever you take your coffee with: halfway through the season, eight teams have a real shot at six playoff spots, and four of them live in the Central, all within a game of each other.

This week the 1 seed plays a road game it's expected to lose, the defending champs get a team that has nothing to lose, and the Magi get the league's lowest scorer, which happens to be the one team that's beaten them six times. Let's go to the board.

The matchups

Win chances come from the site's computer, which plays out the rest of the season 20,000 times. Series records count every meeting since 2019, playoffs included.

Hauk Tua (4-4) at Mailing It In (5-2-1) — game of the week

No game on the slate moves more playoff odds. Hauk Tua sit at 42% and can go to 58% with a win or 29% with a loss. That's a 28-point swing on one Sunday. Mailing goes to 93% with a win and 74% with a loss.

The computer has Mailing a 55% favorite, about as close to a coin flip as it gets. The series is 4-4, but Mailing has won the last three, including a round-one playoff game in 2024 by 55. Hauk Tua put up 153.6 last week, the best score in the league, and left 28.2 from Kirk Cousins on the bench while they did it. The champs just lost on Monday night by 3.6. If you're picking an upset, this is where I'd look.

Bullish on da Bears (6-2) at Thots & Players (4-4)

The 1 seed is a 2-to-1 underdog. Thots are a 67% favorite, and I understand why: 1,022.3 points, second in the league, and an all-play record of 58-30. Bullish are eighth in points at 853.3, with an all-play record of 39-49. Eight weeks in, the computer still doesn't believe in them.

But Bullish just scored 146.8 with Ja'Marr Chase in the lineup, and they're 95% to make the playoffs either way. What they're playing for is the bye: 61% with a win, 27% with a loss. Thots are playing for their footing. They've lost two straight, and a loss drops them to 72% to make it and 4% for a bye. These two have met three times in the playoffs. Thots lead the series 6-5.

Wholey Club (3-5) at The Fist of the Magi (4-4)

The Magi are a 72% favorite, and they need every bit of it. Three straight losses took them from first in the Central to last, and they've averaged 77.7 over that stretch. Win and they're back to 45%; lose and they're at 20%.

Here's the problem. Wholey Club owns this series 6-2 and has won the last two. Wholey is last in points, at 726.2, and averaging 79.7 over its last three, so neither team is scoring right now. Last week I said that if the Magi can't win this one, I'll stop calling them a contender. I'm not taking it back.

Hold Timers (5-3) at Sour Grapes (2-6)

The new Central leader is a 67% favorite and has won three straight, averaging 128.9 in that stretch. Hold Timers lead the series 5-3. A win puts them at 77% to make the playoffs and 38% for a bye. A loss drops them to 50%. In a division this tight, there's no such thing as a safe Sunday. Sour Grapes are at 0.2%, and this is mostly about pride.

Son of Tinactin (3-4-1) at MR. FROBOT (4-4)

FROBOT is the league's top scorer at 1,041.1, 131.0 a game over the last three, and an 80% favorite. They've beaten Son of Tinactin seven straight times and lead the series 8-1. A win puts them at 91% to make the playoffs; a loss, 76%. SOT is at 5%, 15% with a win.

Jesus Christ College (2-6) at Fully Cooked (5-3)

Fully Cooked is a 74% favorite, and nobody in the league has better bye odds, at 40.5%. That goes to 48% with a win and 21% with a loss. Their all-play record of 63-25 is the best in the league. JCC is coming off its second win of the year, and here's one for you: JCC leads this series 7-4.

The playoff picture

Six get in. Division winners take seeds 1–3, the next two by record take 4 and 5, and the 6 seed goes to the most all-play wins among the rest. Seeds 1 and 2 sit out round one.

Mailing It In 5-2-1 2 (West leader) 85% 93% 74% 32%
Hold Timers 5-3 3 (Central leader) 68% 77% 50% 30%

The Central is the story. Hold Timers lead it, and they're the least safe of the three division leaders. FROBOT holds the 5 seed over Thots on total points. Hauk Tua and the Magi are each one game back. And the 5-3 Hold Timers are less likely to make the playoffs than the 4-4 FROBOT, because the computer trusts points more than records. In my day that would've been heresy. Now it's just Tuesday.

The draft board

A week ago Son of Tinactin led Wholey for the 1.01 by 33.1. Now it's 4.9, one good game off somebody's bench. The Magi's slide out of the playoff picture drops them into the lottery at 1.04, and Hold Timers climb out of it.

The extra 1sts are still floating around:

  • Son of Tinactin owns Mailing It In's 1st, projected 1.11. They're in position to open round one and close it.
  • Wholey Club owns Fully Cooked's 1st, projected 1.09, plus their own at 1.02. Wholey wants Fully Cooked out early.
  • Jesus Christ College owns Bullish's 1st, projected 1.12. JCC is rooting for Thots on Sunday.

On the Footballguys superflex big board, Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is still the clear No. 1. Behind him: Florida RB Jadan Baugh, Indiana WR Charlie Becker, Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker, Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy and Miami QB Darian Mensah. Two quarterbacks in the top six, in the first superflex draft this league has ever held. Whoever's picking 1.02 through 1.05 has a decision to make.

Before I go

  • Upset watch: Bullish over Thots (33%). It's not an upset when the 1 seed wins. It just looks like one on paper.
  • Biggest swing: Hauk Tua's playoff odds move 28 points on one game. The Magi's move 25, and Hold Timers' move 27.
  • Points vs. record: FROBOT and Thots are first and second in scoring, and both are 4-4. Bullish is 6-2 on the eighth-most points. I keep saying something has to give. It hasn't yet.
  • Lowest bar: Wholey and the Magi have averaged a combined 157.4 points over their last three weeks. One of them wins Sunday anyway.

See you next week. Bring the coffee.

columns.title: Rumor mill: a seventh playoff spot?
columns.author: rex
columns.teaser: Word out of the league office is that the playoff field could grow to seven teams in 2027, NFL style. One bye, three wild cards, and a seventh seed off the all-play board.
columns.html:
You didn't hear it from me. But I've got people in the league office, and those people say there's been chatter about expanding the playoffs to seven teams in 2027. Nothing's on paper. Nothing's been decided. But they're talking.

What's being floated

The qualifying rules would stay the same, just with one more seat at the table:

  • Seeds 1–3: the three division winners
  • Seeds 4–6: three wild cards on record, up from two
  • Seed 7: the best all-play record among everybody left, the spot the 6 seed fills today

The big change is the bye. Today the top two seeds sit out the first round. Under the new setup only the 1 seed would. That's the NFL's conference bracket: 2 hosts 7, 3 hosts 6, 4 hosts 5, and the 1 seed waits. It's still three rounds, so the title game doesn't move.

If it started this year

As of week 8, here's how it would shake out:

  1. Bullish on da Bears (bye)
  2. Mailing It In vs. 7. Hauk Tua
  3. Hold Timers vs. 6. Thots & Players
  4. Fully Cooked vs. 5. MR. FROBOT

Thots move from the all-play seed to the third wild card on record. Hauk Tua get in as the new 7 seed: they're tied with the Magi in all-play wins, and they've scored more points. The team that would feel it most is Mailing It In. Under today's rules the 2 seed is a week off. Under the new ones, it's a home game against a team that got in through the side door.

Rex's take

More teams, more meaningful December games, more reasons for a 4-4 team to set its lineup. I like it. And make no mistake, this is the NFL's own bracket, which means the bye finally means something: earn the 1 seed or play the extra week.

If you've got an opinion, take it to the commissioner. I'm just telling you what I hear.

columns.title: The Magi fall, the Central flips, and the West forgets how to win
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: The Fist of the Magi go from first in the Central to last, Hold Timers take the division, MR. FROBOT becomes the league's top scorer and Bullish's new receiver makes them the clear class of the East.
columns.html:
I've seen a lot of Week 8s. Most of them sort out a couple of things and leave the rest for November. This one turned over the whole board. A division leader is now in last place. A .500 team has more points than anybody. And the West went 0-4 against the rest of the league in a single weekend.

The Central flips

The Fist of the Magi led the Central all season. They're now in last place. Three straight losses will do that. They scored 88.0, then 74.0, then 71.2 this week, the lowest score in the league. A week ago they held the 3 seed. Today they're on the outside of the playoff picture, and the computer has their playoff chances down from 73% to 38%.

Hold Timers took their spot. Three straight wins and first place in the Central at 5-3. They needed Monday night to get there: D'Andre Swift put up 27.9 for Chicago to beat the defending champs by 3.6.

MR. FROBOT is the best team nobody's talking about. They're 4-4, but they've scored 131 a game over their last three, and their 1,041.1 points are now the most in the league. They hold the 5 seed. All four teams in the Central are within one game of each other, so this division won't be settled for weeks.

The East has a favorite

Bullish on da Bears are 6-2, they hold the 1 seed, and the computer gives them a 95% chance to win the East. Nobody else in that division is above .500.

Bullish have been winning ugly all year: eighth in points, with an all-play record of 39-49. That's why they went and got Ja'Marr Chase, and in his first week he put up 31.1. Bullish scored 146.8, their second-best total of the season. If Chase gives them 25 a week, Bullish stop being the team that wins close and start being the team you don't want to see in December.

The West's lost weekend

All four West teams played someone from another division this week. All four lost. Thots & Players and Sour Grapes have now lost two straight, and Mailing It In and Fully Cooked one each. That's six straight losses across the division.

The West still holds the 2, 4 and 6 seeds, so nobody's panicking yet. But Thots slipped from the 5 seed to the 6, and Mailing lost their hold on the 1 seed to Bullish.

The games

Hold Timers 106.1, Mailing It In 102.5

The game of the week came down to Monday night, with Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba for the champs against Chicago's D'Andre Swift for Hold Timers. Smith-Njigba put up 23.8. Swift put up 27.9. Tony Pollard led Mailing with 28.7, but Hold Timers got the win, the division lead and a three-game winning streak.

Bullish on da Bears 146.8, Fully Cooked 123.4

Chase 31.1, Brock Bowers 28.2, Michael Wilson 26.8. Fully Cooked got 25.4 from Patrick Mahomes and 25.0 from Puka Nacua and still lost by 23. Chase alone outscored every Fully Cooked starter.

Hauk Tua 153.6, Sour Grapes 117.6

The top score of the week. Bhayshul Tuten put up 29.9 and Jahmyr Gibbs 24.8. Hauk Tua even left Kirk Cousins' 28.2 on the bench and still won by 36. They're 4-4 and right back in the Central race.

MR. FROBOT 153.4, Wholey Club 93.6

Joe Burrow scored 39.5, the most by any player this week, and Tee Higgins added 37.5. Two players, 77 points. Wholey Club's best player was the Jacksonville defense.

Jesus Christ College 118.4, Thots & Players 102.3

Tyler Allgeier put up 36.1 for JCC's second win of the year. Thots got 26.6 from Josh Allen, while Cam Ward put up 26.3 on their bench. With one QB slot, there was nowhere to put him. Next year, there will be.

Son of Tinactin 97.4, The Fist of the Magi 71.2

Josh Jacobs scored 23.2 for the Magi. Nobody else on the team cracked 15. Son of Tinactin won without their best two scores of the week: Adonai Mitchell's 27.2 and Jordan Love's 21.5 both sat on the bench.

Next week

Bullish and Thots & Players meet in Week 9, the 1 seed against a team that's lost two straight and needs a win. The Magi get Wholey Club, about as soft a landing as there is. If they can't win that one, I'll stop calling them a contender.

columns.title: Rent now, pay later: grading the trade flurry
columns.author: desk
columns.teaser: Chase to Bullish, McCaffrey to Thots, Cook to Fully Cooked and Breece Hall to Mailing. Our columnists grade every deal, then the analytics desk asks the real question: who can actually keep what they bought?
columns.html:
Four trades in seven days, and three of them sent a playoff contender's 2027 1st out the door. We gave each deal to one of our columnists for a grade on both sides. Then we handed all four to Devin on the analytics desk, who doesn't care about anybody's feelings.

One thing to keep in mind as you read: no pick is locked in yet. Every slot below is a projection from the standings through week 7, and they'll keep moving until the season's over. The same goes for contracts. A salary on the books for 2027 or 2028 only matters if somebody decides the player is worth keeping at that price.

Fully Cooked lands James Cook

POPeg OkaforContracts and cap
  • Fully Cooked get: RB James Cook
  • Wholey Club get: Fully Cooked's 2027 1st (projected 1.09) and $10 of 2027 auction cash

Everybody wants to talk about Cook's 113.6 points in six starts. I want to talk about his contract. He's in year five of a six-year rookie deal at $38. Next year the escalator takes him to $50, at 28, in the last year of the deal. Is a $50 James Cook a keeper? Maybe, if he finishes the way he started. It's close enough that Fully Cooked should treat him as a rental with an option, not a cornerstone.

Is a rental worth a 1st and $10 for a 5-2 team that's third in points? Probably. Cook's been a top back all year, and that pick projects late. But $10 is 5% of an auction budget, and Fully Cooked will feel it in August whether they keep Cook or not.

Wholey Club are 3-4 and dead last in points, so selling makes sense even if it looks like waving the white flag with the playoffs still in reach. They turned a back who's about to get expensive into another 1st and extra auction cash. Wholey's own pick projects to 1.02, Fully Cooked's to 1.09, and they'll have $210 to spend next summer.

Grades: Fully Cooked B · Wholey Club B+

Thots go all in on McCaffrey

Rex CallahanFBP columnist
  • Thots & Players get: RB Christian McCaffrey
  • Sour Grapes get: Thots' 2027 2nd (projected 2.08) and $10 of 2027 auction cash

Flags fly forever. Write it down.

Thots lead the league with 920 points and they're 4-3, which tells you this league isn't always fair. So they went and got the back with 144 points in seven starts. Yes, he's 30. Yes, his hamstring is barking and San Francisco is on bye this week. He's expected back for week 9, and that's all I need to hear in October.

Let's be honest about what this is: a rental. He's $54 next year. If everything breaks right this season, maybe somebody keeps a 31-year-old back at that price. Nobody's keeping him at $60 the year after. So Thots paid a late 2nd and $10 for seven weeks and a playoff run, and for a rental of the league's best-producing back, that's a fair price.

Sour Grapes are 2-5 with a 0.2% chance at the playoffs, and McCaffrey wasn't going to be their keeper either. Turning a player they'd likely have let go into a pick and $10 is exactly what a seller should do.

Grades: Thots & Players B+ · Sour Grapes B

Son of Tinactin cash in on Breece Hall

DWDana WhitlockDynasty desk
  • Mailing It In get: RB Breece Hall
  • Son of Tinactin get: RB RJ Harvey, Mailing's 2027 1st (projected 1.12) and Mailing's 2027 3rd (projected 3.12)

This is how you rebuild. SOT's own pick projects to 1.01 right now, and they just added a second 1st and a 3rd. They also got RJ Harvey: a 25-year-old back at $8, rising to $14 and $23, and very keepable at those prices. Harvey had 76 points this year, mostly from Mailing's bench, and scored 14 in his first start for SOT.

Mailing It In are 5-1-1, the defending champions and the 1 seed, so I understand the impulse. Hall can win a playoff week by himself. But he's out this week with a quad injury, he has 42.5 points this season, and next year he costs $44. On this year's numbers, that's not a keeper unless he comes back strong. So Mailing may have rented a hurt back for two months, and paid for it with a 1st, a 3rd and the cheap young back they could have kept for years.

Mailing are buying a December, and SOT just bought three years.

Grades: Son of Tinactin A · Mailing It In C+

Bullish buy Ja'Marr Chase

Sal FerraroFBP columnist
  • Bullish on da Bears get: WR Ja'Marr Chase, their own 2027 3rd back (projected 3.11) and MR. FROBOT's 2027 4th (projected 4.07)
  • Jesus Christ College get: Bullish's 2027 1st (projected 1.11), Bullish's 2028 2nd and $5 of 2027 auction cash

Sixteen years on this beat, and I've learned one thing about first-place teams that rank eighth in scoring: they either go get somebody or they go home. Bullish went and got somebody. Ja'Marr Chase is 26 and he's put up 97 points in six starts for a team that was losing anyway.

Now, the kid next to me made me look at the contract, and he's right. Chase is $62 this year, $65 next year and $71 after that. Nobody's keeping him at $71, and $65 is a stretch. So this is a rental, and Bullish paid a 1st, a future 2nd and five bucks for seven weeks and a playoff run, while getting two picks back. For a team that wants a ring, I'll take that.

Here's where I change my mind on JCC. I wanted to yell at them for selling a young WR1. But they weren't keeping him at those prices either. A 1-6 team turning a player they'd have let go into a 1st, a 2nd and $5 isn't a fire sale. It's housekeeping.

Grades: Bullish on da Bears B+ · Jesus Christ College B

The analytics desk: who can keep what they bought?

Devin ChoAnalytics desk

Grades are nice. Here's what each side actually took on. I scored every trade two ways.

This season: the starter points each buyer expects to add over the last seven weeks of the regular season. Each projection blends a player's 2025 and 2026 per-game scoring and skips games he's already listed out for.

Next two seasons: what each side has that's worth keeping in 2027 and 2028.

  • Players: a player only counts in a future year if his projected points beat what his salary would buy at the auction. This year, a dollar spent on a starter at the auction has bought about 4.5 points. If he isn't worth keeping, he counts for nothing that year, because his owner just lets him go. Running backs lose 10% a year from 28 and 20% from 30.
  • Picks: worth what that slot has actually produced in this league, minus the rookie salary. They're projected slots, so they'll move. FBP rookies drafted from 2021 to 2024 scored this many points in their first two seasons:
Slot Avg. points, first 2 seasons
1.09–1.12 148
Late 2nd 91
Any 2nd 101
Late 3rd 62
Mid 4th 19
  • Auction cash: counted at the same 4.5 points a dollar, so $10 is worth 45 points.

Here's the keeper check for every player who moved:

Player 2027 salary Keep? 2028 salary Keep?
Ja'Marr Chase $65 No $71 No
Christian McCaffrey $54 Coin flip $60 No
James Cook $50 Coin flip — Deal ends
Breece Hall $44 Probably not $50 No
RJ Harvey $14 Yes $23 Yes

Four of the five are rentals or coin flips, and the one sure keeper in the bunch went to a rebuilding team.

Trade Buyer, this season Buyer, next 2 seasons Seller, next 2 seasons Future paid per point now
McCaffrey Thots +129 −45 +109 1.2
Chase Bullish +112 +32 +208 1.6
Cook Fully Cooked +125 −45 +157 1.6
Hall Mailing +78 0 +312 4.0

The last column is the price tag. It's how many points of future value each buyer gave up for every point it adds this season. Lower is a better deal.

The sellers win all four on future value. That's how a rental works: you trade next year for this year. The real question is who paid a fair price.

Thots got the best rental. McCaffrey adds the most points this season, about 21 a week, and Thots paid the least for him. Bullish and Fully Cooked paid about the same price, around 16 to 18 points a week for 1.6 points of future value each. Bullish at least got two picks back.

Mailing paid more than three times what Thots did. Hall is hurt and probably not a keeper, and the deal also cost them Harvey, the only real keeper who moved all week. For the defending champs that buys a better playoff ceiling, and little else.

And Sal: welcome to the spreadsheet.

Devin's winners: this season, Thots, Bullish and Fully Cooked. Next two seasons, Son of Tinactin by a mile, then Jesus Christ College, Wholey Club and Sour Grapes. Biggest overpay: Mailing.

Points through week 7. Salaries and contract years from MFL; auction cash from the league's budget ledger. Pick history covers the 2021–2024 rookie drafts. Playoff weeks aren't counted. Keeper calls are projections. A great second half can turn a coin flip into a keeper.

columns.title: Six teams, two byes, and a race to the bottom nobody can rig
columns.author: sal
columns.teaser: Defending champ Mailing It In draws the hottest team in the league, Fully Cooked and Bullish fight for a bye, and the kid in the next seat keeps telling me Bullish is a fraud. He might be right.
columns.html:
Sixteen years I've been covering this league, and the first thing they teach you is this: look at the standings. The second thing, they teach you now, is don't trust them. Half the league is separated by one game, and the other half is already staring at the draft board. Six teams sit at 4-3 or better, and only two of them get byes.

Defending champion Mailing It In (5-1-1) holds the 1 seed on a five-game win streak. Week 8 hands them the one team nobody wants to see right now. And Fully Cooked goes into East leader Bullish's building with a bye on the line. Let's go to the board.

The matchups

The win chances come from the site's computer, which plays out the rest of the season 20,000 times. I didn't trust it either. It's been annoyingly right. Series records count every meeting since 2019, playoffs included.

Fully Cooked (5-2) at Bullish on da Bears (5-2) — game of the week

The computer makes Fully Cooked a 72% favorite, and I can't argue. They've won three straight by an average of 36. Bullish leads the East at 5-2, but their 706.5 points rank eighth of 12, and their all-play record is 30-47. In my day we called that "winning ugly." Now they call it "unsustainable," and I hate that they're probably right.

Bullish does own this series, six wins in eight meetings. A Fully Cooked win pushes their bye chances to 47%. A Bullish win keeps their bye hopes alive at 30%, and they're 86% to win the East either way.

Mailing It In (5-1-1) at Hold Timers (4-3)

The closest game on the board: Mailing a 56% favorite. Hold Timers are the hottest team in the league, averaging 132 over the last three weeks and winning their last two by 76 and 55. Mailing has won eight of ten meetings, and champions know how to play in somebody else's barn. But this one moves Hold Timers' playoff odds 28 points — 76% with a win, 48% with a loss. Nobody on the slate has more riding on a single Sunday.

Thots & Players (4-3) at Jesus Christ College (1-6)

Thots lead the league in points (920.0) and the power rankings, and they're 4-3. Explain that one to me. They're an 80% favorite against a JCC team that has lost six straight and averaged 94 over its last three. Thots lead the series 7-5. Win and they're 95.5% to make the playoffs; lose and they drop to 84.5%.

The Fist of the Magi (4-3) at Son of Tinactin (2-4-1)

Fist is a 78% favorite, but they've dropped two straight, including a 74-point clunker in week 7. They lead the Central only on the total-points tiebreak, so this one matters: a win lifts their playoff odds to 77.5%, a loss sinks them to 55%. SOT leads the series 4-3 and needs this just to stay in double digits (11.6% with a win, 2.8% with a loss).

MR. FROBOT (3-4) at Wholey Club (3-4)

FROBOT is the fourth-best scoring team in the league sitting at 3-4, holding the 6 seed on all-play wins, and an 80% favorite. Wholey has the league's lowest point total (632.6) and won last week by two-tenths of a point. I've seen a lot of football. I have not seen much of that. FROBOT leads the series 5-3; win and it's 77% playoff odds, lose and it's 57%.

Sour Grapes (2-5) at Hauk Tua (3-4)

Hauk Tua is a 66% favorite sitting at 17% playoff odds, so call it a must-win: 21% with a win, 7.5% with a loss. Sour Grapes has scored under 100 in two of its last three and is at 0.2% to make it. The series is tied 4-4, which is the most interesting thing I can tell you about this one.

The playoff picture

Six get in. Division winners take seeds 1–3, the next two by record take 4 and 5, and the 6 seed goes to the most all-play wins among the rest. Seeds 1 and 2 sit out round one.

Bullish on da Bears 5-2 2 (East leader) 87% 95% 84% 15%

Hold Timers are the hard-luck story: 4-3 and on the outside, behind Fist for the Central on total points, with the wild cards going to Fully Cooked's record and Thots' points. And here's the part that would've gotten me laughed out of the press box in 2019: Thots and Fully Cooked look safer than two of the division leaders.

The draft board

Now, the bottom. Every year somebody asks me who's tanking. Every year I tell them the same thing: you can't, not here. Non-playoff teams pick in order of lowest potential points — the best lineup you could have started every week. Losing doesn't move you up. A bad roster does. Son of Tinactin holds the 1.01 today.

Picks 1.07–1.12 go to the playoff teams, worst finish to best.

What makes this year fun is the extra picks floating around:

  • Son of Tinactin owns Mailing It In's 1st from the Breece Hall trade, projected 1.12. SOT could open round one and close it.
  • Wholey Club owns Fully Cooked's 1st from the James Cook deal, projected 1.09. Wholey ought to be pulling for Bullish this week, and for an early Fully Cooked playoff exit.
  • Jesus Christ College owns Bullish's 1st from the Ja'Marr Chase trade, projected 1.11. JCC wants the opposite.

The prize at the top is Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith, the clear consensus 1.01 in the early superflex rookie rankings. After him it bunches up: Texas WR Cam Coleman, Florida RB Jadan Baugh, Texas QB Arch Manning and Indiana WR Charlie Becker all average between picks 4 and 6. Picks 1.02 through 1.05 are where the real decisions happen, and Wholey, Sour Grapes and JCC are separated by one good week apiece.
